s.d: ἀρέσκω [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] 1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): with dative of person(s), [[matthew 14 6|Mat.14:6]], [[mark 6 22|Mrk.6:22]], [[romans 8 8|Rom.8:8 15:2]], [[1-thessalonians 2 15|1Th.2:15 4:1]], [[1-corinthians 7 32|1Co.7:32-34]] [[galatians 1 10|Gal.1:10]], [[2-timothy 2 4|2Ti.2:4]]; before ἐνώπισν (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 65. 2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (see M, Th., ICC, 1 Co., ll with; Cremer, 640 f.); [[romans 15 1|Rom.15:1]], 3, [[1-corinthians 10 33|1Co.10:33]], [[1-thessalonians 2 4|1Th.2:4]].† (AS)

ἀρεστός, -ή, -όν (ἀρέσκω), [in LXX for יָשָׁר, etc. ;] pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; see Cremer, 641 f; MM, see word): with dative of person(s), [[john 8 29|Jhn.8:29]], [[acts 12 3|Act.12:3]]; before ἐνώπιον, with genitive (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), [[1-john 3 22|1Jn.3:22;]] ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf (El., § 69, 5; 72, 5), [[acts 6 2|Act.6:2.]]† (AS)

Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ, Aretas, an Arabian king: [[2-corinthians 11 32|2Co.11:32]] (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").† (AS)

ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX, in sing.: [[habakkuk 3 3|Hab.3:3]], [[zechariah 6 13|Zec.6:13]] (הוֹד), in pl.: [[isaiah 42 8|Isa.42:8, 12 43:21 63:7]] (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.4:1 5:13 8:7 2:1-24; 4Mac.2.2 * ;] prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue; (a) of God: [[2-peter 1 3|2Pe.1:3;]] (b) of men: [[philippians 4 8|Php.4:8]], [[2-peter 1 5|2Pe.1:5]]; pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies: [[1-peter 2 9|1Pe.2:9]] (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; see Hort, 1 Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95 f., thinks it means manifestations of divine power, as in current Gk. speech; cf. also MM, see word)† (AS)
ἀρήν, ἀρνός, ὁ (nom, not in use, exc. in early times: see MM, see word), [in LXX for מְרִיא, כֶּבֶשׂ, etc. ;] a lamb: [[luke 10 3|Luk.10:3.]]† (AS)
ἀριθμέω, -ῶ [in LXX for סָפַר pi., פָּקַד pi., etc. ;] to number (esp. for payment, MM, see word): [[matthew 10 30|Mat.10:30]], [[luke 12 7|Luk.12:7]], [[revelation 7 9|Rev.7:9]].† (AS)

ἀριθμός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מִסְפָּר ;] number, a number: [[luke 22 3|Luk.22:3]], [[john 6 10|Jhn.6:10]], [[acts 4 4|Act.4:4 5:36 6:7 11:21 16:5]], [[romans 9 27|Rom.9:27]], [[revelation 5 11|Rev.5:11 7:4 9:16 13:17-18 15:2 20:8]] (for exx. of mystical use in π., see MM, see word).† (AS)

Ἁριμαθεία (WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Ἁριμαθάιμ, [[1-samuel 1 1|1Ki.1:1]], al. (רָמָה) ;] Arimathæa: [[matthew 27 57|Mat.27:57]], [[mark 15 43|Mrk.15:43]], [[luke 23 51|Luk.23:51]], [[john 19 38|Jhn.19:38]].† (AS)
Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ (ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling) Aristarchus: [[acts 19 29|Act.19:29 20:4 27:2]], [[colossians 4 10|Col.4:10]], Phm 24 (AS)

ἀριστάω, -ῶ (ἄριστον), [in LXX: [[genesis 43 25|Gen.43:25]] (לֶחֶם אָכַל), [[1-samuel 14 24|1Ki.14:24]] (לֶחֶם), [[1-kings 13 7|3Ki.13:7]] (סָעַד), Tob.2:1 * ;] 1. prop., to breakfast: [[john 21 12|Jhn.21:12, 15]] 2. In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: [[luke 11 37|Luk.11:37.]]† (AS)

ἀριστερός, -ά, -όν [in LXX for שְׂמֹאול ;] left, on the left: ὅπλα, [[2-corinthians 6 7|2Co.6:7;]] ἡ ἀ.. (sc. χείρ), [[matthew 6 3|Mat.6:3;]] ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left (MM, see word ): [[mark 10 37|Mrk.10:37]], [[luke 23 33|Luk.23:33]].† (AS)
Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ (ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling) Aristobulus, a Christian: [[romans 16 10|Rom.16:10.]]† (AS)

ἄριστον, -ου, τό [in LXX: [[1-kings 3 1|3Ki.3:1]] (לֶחֶם), Tob.2:1, 4, al. ;] 1 1, prop., breakfast. 2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: [[matthew 22 4|Mat.22:4]], [[luke 11 38|Luk.11:38 14:12]].† (AS)

ἀρκετός, -ή, -όν (ἀρκέω), [in Aq.: [[deuteronomy 25 2|Deu.25:2]] * ;] sufficient: [[matthew 6 34|Mat.6:34]] (on the neut., see B1., § 31, 2); before ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), [[matthew 10 25|Mat.10:25;]] with inf., [[1-peter 4 3|1Pe.4:3]] (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, see word).† (AS)

ἀρκέω, -ῶ [in LXX for הוֹן, etc. ;] 1. to keep off; with dative, to assist. 2. to suffice: with dative of person(s), Jo 67, [[2-corinthians 12 9|2Co.12:9;]] impers., [[matthew 25 9|Mat.25:9]], [[john 14 8|Jhn.14:8]] (MM, see word). Pass., to be satisfied: with dative of thing(s), [[luke 3 14|Luk.3:14]], [[1-timothy 6 8|1Ti.6:8]], [[hebrews 13 5|Heb.13:5]]; before ἐπί, III Jn 10.† (AS)
ἅρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב ;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ, a bear: [[revelation 13 2|Rev.13:2.]] (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)† (AS)
ἅρμα, -τος, τό (ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רָכַב ;] a chariot: [[acts 8 28|Act.8:28-29, 38]], [[revelation 9 9|Rev.9:9]].† (AS)

Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, [[2-chronicles 35 22|2Ch.35:22]], Μαγεδώ, [[judges 1 27|Jdg.1:27;]] Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): [[revelation 16 16|Rev.16:16]] (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).† Ἅρ, indecl., [[revelation 16 16|Rev.16:16]], see, Ἁρμαγεδών Μαγεδών, Magedon: [[revelation 16 16|Rev.16:16]] (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).† (AS)

ἁρμόζω (ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc. ;] 1. to fit, join. 2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid., (a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: [[2-corinthians 11 2|2Co.11:2]] (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).† (AS)
ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Sir.27:2, 4Ma.10:5 * ;] a joining, joint: [[hebrews 4 12|Heb.4:12.]]† (AS)

ἀρνέομαι -οῦμαι, depon., [in LXX: [[genesis 18 15|Gen.18:15]] (כָּחַשׁ pi.), Wis.12:27 16:16 17:10, 4Ma.8:7 4Mac 10:15 * ;] 1. to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., [[matthew 26 70|Mat.26:70]], [[luke 8 45|Luk.8:45]]; before ἅτι, [[1-john 2 22|1Jn.2:22;]] with inf., [[hebrews 11 24|Heb.11:24]] 2. In late Gk. (MM, see word), with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: [[acts 3 14|Act.3:14 7:35]]; Ἰησοῦν, [[matthew 10 33|Mat.10:33]], [[2-timothy 2 12|2Ti.2:12]], [[1-john 2 22|1Jn.2:22]], Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, [[luke 9 23|Luk.9:23]], [[2-timothy 2 13|2Ti.2:13]] (prove false to) 3. C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure: [[1-timothy 5 8|1Ti.5:8]], [[titus 2 12|Tit.2:12]], [[2-timothy 3 5|2Ti.3:5]] (cf. ἀπαρνέομαι) (AS)

ἀρνίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ἀρήν; see MM, see word), [in LXX: [[psalms 114 4|Psa.114:4]], 6 (pl., צֹאן בֵּן), [[jeremiah 11 19|Jer.11:19]] (כֶּבֶשׂ), [[jeremiah 50 45|Jer.50:45]] (צָעִיר)* ;] a little lamb, a lamb: [[john 21 15|Jhn.21:15]], [[revelation 2 7|Rev.2:7]].† (AS)

ἀροτριάω, -ῶ (ἄροτρον), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 22 10|Deu.22:10]], al. (חָרַשׁ), [[isaiah 7 25|Isa.7:25]] (עֲדַר) ;] later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, see word): [[luke 17 7|Luk.17:7]], [[1-corinthians 9 10|1Co.9:10]].† (AS)
ἄροτρον, -ου, τό (ἀρόω, to plough), [in LXX chiefly for אֵת ;] a plough: [[luke 9 62|Luk.9:62.]]† (AS)
ἁρπαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἁρπάζω), [in LXX (as also ἅρπαγμα) for גָּזֵל, etc. ;] pillage, plundering, robbery: [[matthew 23 25|Mat.23:25]], [[luke 11 39|Luk.11:39]], [[hebrews 10 34|Heb.10:34]].† (AS)

ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ (ἁρπάζω); 1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), [[philippians 2 6|Php.2:6]], AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word). 2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα ([[ezekiel 22 25|Eze.22:25]], of a lion's prey, ), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, see word, esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. [[romans 11 9|Rom.11:9]], where cf. LXX; [[1-corinthians 13 9|1Co.13:9]], 2 Co 19), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, ll with† (AS)

ἁρπάζω [in LXX chiefly for גָּזַל, טָרַף ;] to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 12 29|Mat.12:29 13:19]], [[john 10 12|Jhn.10:12, 28-29]]; τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, [[matthew 11 12|Mat.11:12;]] with accusative of person(s), [[john 6 15|Jhn.6:15]], [[acts 8 39|Act.8:39 23:10]], Ju 23; pass., before ἕως, [[2-corinthians 12 2|2Co.12:2;]] εἰς, [[2-corinthians 12 4|2Co.12:4]], [[1-thessalonians 4 17|1Th.4:17]]; πρός, [[revelation 12 5|Rev.12:5]] (cf. δι-, συν-αρπάζω, and see MM, see word).† (AS)

ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ (ἁρπάζω), [in LXX: [[genesis 49 27|Gen.49:27]] (טָרַף) * ;] rapacious: [[matthew 7 15|Mat.7:15]], [[luke 18 11|Luk.18:11]]; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, see word), [[1-corinthians 5 10|1Co.5:10-11 6:10]].† (AS)

ἀρραβών (T, ἀραβ-: 2Co, ll. with), -ώνος, ὁ, [in LXX: [[genesis 38 17|Gen.38:17-20]] (עֲרָבוֹן)* ;] an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: [[2-corinthians 1 22|2Co.1:22 5:5]], [[ephesians 1 14|Eph.1:14]]. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phænicians (AR, Eph., l.with). It is found in π. with both spellings (see Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; see MM, see word)† (AS)
ἄραφος, -ον (Rec. ἄρραφο), (ῥάπτω, to sew) without seam: [[john 19 23|Jhn.19:23.]]† (AS)

ἄρσην (ἄρρην, T, in [[romans 1 27|Rom.1:27;]] Rec. in [[revelation 12 5|Rev.12:5, 13]]) -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό (old Attic for ἄρρην, see supr.; both forms are found in π.; MM, see word), [in LXX chiefly for זָכָר ;] male: [[matthew 19 4|Mat.19:4]], [[mark 10 6|Mrk.10:6]], [[luke 2 23|Luk.2:23]], [[romans 1 27|Rom.1:27]], [[galatians 3 28|Gal.3:28]], [[revelation 12 5|Rev.12:5, 13]].† (AS)

ἄρρητος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: [[leviticus 18 23|Lev.18:23]] * ;] 1. unspoken (Hom., al.). 2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; frequently in Inscr.; MM, see word): [[2-corinthians 12 4|2Co.12:4.]]† (AS)

ἄρρωστος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: [[1-kings 14 5|3Ki.14:5]]Α, [[malachi 1 8|Mal.1:8]] (חָלָה), Sir.7:35 * ;] feeble, sickly: [[matthew 14 14|Mat.14:14]], [[mark 6 5|Mrk.6:5, 13 16:18]], [[1-corinthians 11 30|1Co.11:30]].† (AS)
ἀρσενοκοίτης, -ου, ὁ (ἄρσην, κοιτή), a sodomite: [[1-corinthians 6 9|1Co.6:9]], [[1-timothy 1 10|1Ti.1:10]].† (AS)
Ἀρτεμᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ Artemas: [[titus 3 12|Tit.3:12.]]† (AS)
Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: [[acts 19 24|Act.19:24, 27-28]] (AS)
ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ (ἀρτάω, to fasten to), a fore-sail or top-sail: [[acts 27 40|Act.27:40]] (see DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, see word).† (AS)

ἄρτι adv., [in LXX: Dan LXX 9:22 10:11 (עַתָּה), al. ;] adv., of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future, just, just now, this moment: [[matthew 3 15|Mat.3:15 9:18 26:53]], [[john 13 7|Jhn.13:7]], [[galatians 4 20|Gal.4:20]], [[1-thessalonians 3 6|1Th.3:6]] (see Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l), [[revelation 12 10|Rev.12:10;]] opposite to past time, [[john 9 19|Jhn.9:19, 25 13:33]], [[1-corinthians 16 7|1Co.16:7]], [[galatians 1 9|Gal.1:9-10]]; to future, [[john 13 37|Jhn.13:37 16:12, 31]], [[1-corinthians 13 12|1Co.13:12]], [[2-thessalonians 2 7|2Th.2:7]], [[1-peter 1 6|1Pe.1:6 1:8]]; ἄχρι τῆς ἅ. ὥρας, [[1-corinthians 4 11|1Co.4:11;]] ἕως ἄ., [[matthew 11 12|Mat.11:12]], [[john 2 10|Jhn.2:10 5:17 16:24]], [[1-corinthians 4 13|1Co.4:13 8:7 15:6]], [[1-john 2 9|1Jn.2:9]]; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., see: ἀπάρτι (see Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, see word).† SYN.: νῦν, now, "the objective, immediate present; ἤδη, now, already, " the subjective present, with a suggested reference to some other time or to some expectation". (Thayer, 75.) (AS)
ἀρτι-γέννητος, -ον (ἄρτι, γεννάω), new-born: [[1-peter 2 2|1Pe.2:2]] (Luc.).† (AS)
ἄρτιος, -α, -ον fitted, complete: [[2-timothy 3 17|2Ti.3:17]] (MM, see word).† (AS)

ἄρτος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for לֶחֶם ;] bread, a loaf: [[matthew 4 3|Mat.4:3]], 4 [[mark 3 20|Mrk.3:20]], al.; ἄρτοι τ. προθέσεως, bread of the setting forth, i.e. the shewbread. Metaphorical, ὁ ἄ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. ζωῆς, ref. to Christ, [[john 6 33|Jhn.6:33, 35]]; in general, food: [[matthew 6 11|Mat.6:11]], al.; ἄ. φαγεῖν (Heb. אֲכֹל לֶחֶם), to eat (MM, see word), [[luke 14 1|Lu 14:1]], al. (AS)

ἀρτύω [in Sm.: [[song-of-solomon 8 2|Sng.8:2]] * ;] 1. to arrange, make ready (Hom.). 2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, see word): [[mark 9 50|Mrk.9:50]], [[luke 14 34|Luk.14:34]], [[colossians 4 6|Col.4:6]].† (AS)
Ἀρφαξάδ, ὁ(Heb. אַרְפַּכְשַׁד), Arphaxad: [[luke 3 36|Luk.3:36.]]† (AS)
ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ (ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος), archangel, a chief angel: [[1-thessalonians 4 16|1Th.4:16]], Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, see word).† (AS)

ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον (ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם ;] original, ancient: [[matthew 5 21|Mat.5:21, 33]], [[luke 9 8|Luk.9:8, 19]], [[acts 15 7|Act.15:7, 21 21:16]], [[2-corinthians 5 17|2Co.5:17]], [[2-peter 2 5|2Pe.2:5]], [[revelation 12 9|Rev.12:9 20:2]].† SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, see word). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος (see Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116) (AS)
Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judma, Samaria and Idumæa: [[matthew 2 22|Mat.2:22.]]† (AS)

ἀρχή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for קֶדֶם, רֹאשׁ, רֹאשׁ, etc. ;] 1. beginning, origin; (a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, [[revelation 21 6|Rev.21:6]] (cf. 18); similarly, of Christ, [[revelation 22 13|Rev.22:13;]] of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, [[revelation 3 14|Rev.3:14;]] in his relation to the Church, [[colossians 1 18|Col.1:18;]] ἐν ἀ., [[john 1 1|Jhn.1:1-2;]] ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), [[matthew 19 4|Mat.19:4, 8 24:21]], [[mark 10 6|Mrk.10:6 13:19]], [[john 8 44|Jhn.8:44]], [[2-thessalonians 2 13|2Th.2:13]], [[2-peter 3 4|2Pe.3:4]], [[1-john 1 1|1Jn.1:1]] [[john 2 13|Jn 2:13-14]] [[john 2 24|Jn 2:24]]; κατ ἀρχἀς, [[hebrews 1 10|Heb.1:10;]] (b) relatively: [[hebrews 7 3|Heb.7:3;]] ἀ. ὠδίνων, [[matthew 24 8|Mat.24:8]], [[mark 13 9|Mrk.13:9]]; τ. σημείων, [[john 2 11|Jhn.2:11;]] τ. ὑποστάσεως, [[hebrews 3 14|Heb.3:14;]] τ. λογίων, [[hebrews 5 12|Heb.5:12;]] ὁ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγος, the account of the beginning, the elementary view of Christ, [[hebrews 6 1|Heb.6:1;]] ἀρχὴν λαμβάνειν, to begin, [[hebrews 2 3|Heb.2:3;]] ἐξ ἀ., [[john 6 64|Jhn.6:64 16:4]]; ἀπ᾽ ἀ., [[luke 1 2|Luk.1:2]], [[john 15 27|Jhn.15:27]], [[1-john 2 7|1Jn.2:7]] [[john 2 24|Jn 2:24]] [[john 3 11|Jn 3:11]], 2Jn.5-6; ἐν ἀ., [[acts 11 15|Act.11:15 26:4]], [[philippians 4 15|Php.4:15]]; τὴν ἀρχήν, adverbially, at all (Hdt., al.; v MM, see word): [[john 8 25|Jhn.8:25.]] 2. an extremity, a corner: [[acts 10 11|Act.10:11 11:5]]. 3. sovereignty, principality, rule (cf. DB, i, 616 f.): [[luke 12 11|Luk.12:11 20:20]], [[romans 8 38|Rom.8:38]], [[1-corinthians 15 24|1Co.15:24]], [[ephesians 1 21|Eph.1:21 3:10 6:12]], [[colossians 1 16|Col.1:16 2:10, 15]] [[titus 3 1|Tit.3:1]], Ju 6 (Cremer, 113).† (AS)

ἀρχηγός, -όν [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, נָשִׂיא etc. ;] beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.; 1. founder, author (Lat. auchor; so some­times in π., see MM, see word; Milligan, NTD, 75): [[acts 3 15|Act.3:15]] (R, mg.), [[hebrews 2 10|Heb.2:10]] (R, txt.; but see Westc., in l, and Page, Ac., l.with). 2. prince, leader (so in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 153): [[acts 3 15|Act.3:15]] (R, txt.) [[acts 5 31|Act.5:31]], [[hebrews 2 10|Heb.2:10]] (cf. R, mg.) 122 (Cremer, 117).† (AS)
ἀρχ-ιερατικός, -ή, -όν (ἀρχιερύς), high-priestly: [[acts 4 6|Act.4:6]] (AS)

ἀρχιερεύς, -έως, ὁ, [in LXX for כּ'' הָרֹאשׁ,כּ'' הַגָּדוֹל ,כּהֵן ;] 1. high-priest: [[mark 2 26|Mrk.2:26 14:47]], al.; of Christ: [[hebrews 2 17|Heb.2:17 3:1]], al. 2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: [[matthew 2 4|Mat.2:4]], [[mark 8 31|Mrk.8:31]], al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297f.; MM, see word). (AS)

ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ [in Sm.: [[2-kings 3 4|4Ki.3:4]] * ;] found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, [[1-peter 5 4|1Pe.5:4.]]† (AS)
Ἄρχιππος, -ου, ὁ Archippus: [[colossians 4 17|Col.4:17]], Phm 2.† (AS)

ἀρχισυνάγωγος, -ου, ὁ (συναγωγή), ruler of a synagogue, an administrative officer, supervising the worship (הַכְּנֵםֶת רֹאשׁ): [[mark 5 22|Mrk.5:22, 35-36 5:38]] [[luke 8 49|Luk.8:49 13:14]], [[acts 13 15|Act.13:15 18:8, 17]] (Inscr., see MM, see word; cf. also DB, ext., 101).† (AS)

ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ (τέκτων), [in LXX: [[isaiah 3 3|Isa.3:3]] (חָרָשׁ) Sir.38:27. 2Ma.2:29 * ;] a master-builder, architect: [[1-corinthians 3 10|1Co.3:10]] (in π. of building contractors, MM, see word).† (AS)
ἀρχι-τελώνης, -ου, ὁ a chief tax-collector, chief publican: [[luke 19 2|Luk.19:2.]]† (AS)
ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ (τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches) the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): [[john 2 8|Jhn.2:8-9.]]† (AS)

ἄρχω [in LXX for חָלַל, מָשַׁל, etc. ;] 1. to begin. 2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, [[mark 10 42|Mrk.10:42]], [[romans 15 12|Rom.15:12]]. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, [[matthew 16 21|Mat.16:21 20:8]], [[luke 14 18|Luk.14:18 23:5 24:27, 47]], [[john 8 9|Jhn.8:9]], [[acts 1 22|Act.1:22 8:35 10:37]], [[1-peter 4 17|1Pe.4:17]]; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45 2:23 5:17]], [[luke 3 8|Luk.3:8]], al. (see M, [[proverbs 14 1|Pro.14:1-35]] f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word) (AS)

ἄρχω [in LXX for חָלַל, מָשַׁל, etc. ;] 1. to begin. 2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, [[mark 10 42|Mrk.10:42]], [[romans 15 12|Rom.15:12]]. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, [[matthew 16 21|Mat.16:21 20:8]], [[luke 14 18|Luk.14:18 23:5 24:27, 47]], [[john 8 9|Jhn.8:9]], [[acts 1 22|Act.1:22 8:35 10:37]], [[1-peter 4 17|1Pe.4:17]]; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45 2:23 5:17]], [[luke 3 8|Luk.3:8]], al. (see M, [[proverbs 14 1|Pro.14:1-35]] f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word) (AS)

ἄρχων, -οντος, ὁ (present ptcp. of ἄρχω), [in LXX for נָשִׂיא., רֹאשׁ, שַׂר, etc. ;] a ruler, chief: Jesus, [[revelation 1 5|Rev.1:5;]] rulers of nations, [[matthew 20 25|Mat.20:25]], [[acts 4 26|Act.4:26 7:35]]; magistrates, [[acts 23 5|Act.23:5]], [[romans 13 3|Rom.13:3]]; judges, [[luke 12 58|Luk.12:58]], [[acts 7 27|Act.7:27, 35 16:19]]; members of the Sanhedrin, [[luke 14 1|Luk.14:1 23:13, 35 24:20]], [[john 3 1|Jhn.3:1 7:26, 48 12:42]], [[acts 3 17|Act.3:17 4:5, 8 13:27 14:5]]; rulers of synagogues, [[matthew 9 18|Mat.9:18, 23]], [[luke 8 41|Luk.8:41 18:18]]; οἱ ἄ. τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, [[1-corinthians 2 6|1Co.2:6-8;]] of the devil: ἄ. τῶν δαιμονίων, [[matthew 9 34|Mat.9:34 12:24]], [[mark 3 22|Mrk.3:22]], [[luke 11 15|Luk.11:15]]; ὁ ἄ. τοῦ κόσμου, [[john 12 31|Jhn.12:31 14:30 16:11]]; ἄ. τ. ἐξουσίας τ. ἀέρος, [[ephesians 2 2|Eph.2:2]] (MM, see word; DB, iii, 838; Ext., 99 f; DCG, ii, 419; DCG, see word Archon).† (AS)
ἄρωμα, -τος, τό [in LXX for בֶּשֶׂם ;] spice: [[mark 16 1|Mrk.16:1]], [[luke 23 56|Luk.23:56 24:1]], [[john 19 40|Jhn.19:40]].† (AS)
Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף), [H609] Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: [[matthew 1 7|Mat.1:7-8.]]† (AS)

ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον (σαλεύω), [in LXX: [[exodus 13 16|Exo.13:16]], [[deuteronomy 6 8|Deu.6:8 11:18]] (טוֹפָפָה)* ;] unmoved, immovable: [[acts 27 41|Act.27:41;]] metaphorically, [[hebrews 12 28|Heb.12:28.]]† (AS)

ἄ-σβεστος, -ον (σβέννυμι), [in LXX for נָפַח לֹא, [[job 20 26|Job.20:26]] א3 A (ἄκαυστον, א2 B)* ;] unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, [[matthew 3 12|Mat.3:12]], [[mark 9 43|Mrk.9:43]], [[luke 3 17|Luk.3:17]].† (AS)

ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc. ;] ungodliness, impiety: [[romans 1 18|Rom.1:18 11:26]], [[2-timothy 2 16|2Ti.2:16]], [[titus 2 12|Tit.2:12]]; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, see word).† (AS)
ἀσεβέω, -ῶ (ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פָּשַׁע, רָשַׁע ;] to be ungodly, act profanely: [[2-peter 2 6|2Pe.2:6;]] with cogn. accusative (MM, see word), Ju 15.† (AS)

ἀσεβής, -ές (σέβω, to reverence), [in LXX chiefly for רָשַׁע ;] un­godly, impious: [[romans 4 5|Rom.4:5 5:6]], [[1-timothy 1 9|1Ti.1:9]], [[1-peter 4 18|1Pe.4:18]], [[2-peter 2 5|2Pe.2:5-6 3:7]], Ju 4 15.† (AS)

ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσελγής, licentious; see MM, see word), [in LXX: Wis.14:26, 3Ma.2:26 * ;] licentiousness, wantonness, excess: [[mark 7 22|Mrk.7:22]], [[romans 13 13|Rom.13:13]], [[2-corinthians 12 21|2Co.12:21]], [[galatians 5 19|Gal.5:19]] (Lft., in l), [[ephesians 4 19|Eph.4:19]], [[1-peter 4 3|1Pe.4:3]], [[2-peter 2 2|2Pe.2:2 2:7 2:18]], Ju 4.† SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (see Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46). (AS)

ἄσημος, -ον (σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: [[genesis 30 42|Gen.30:42]] (עָטַף), [[job 42 11|Job.42:11]], 3Ma.1:3 * ;] without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, see word). Metaphorical (MM, see word), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, [[acts 21 39|Act.21:39.]]† (AS)
Ἀσήρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָשֵׁר), Asher: [[luke 2 36|Luk.2:36]], [[revelation 7 6|Rev.7:6]].† (AS)

ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;] weakness, frailty, sickness: [[luke 13 11|Luk.13:11-12]], [[john 11 4|Jhn.11:4]], [[acts 28 9|Act.28:9]], [[romans 6 19|Rom.6:19 8:26]], [[2-corinthians 11 30|2Co.11:30 13:4]], [[galatians 4 13|Gal.4:13]] (MM, see word), [[hebrews 5 2|Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34]]; ἐν ἀ., [[john 5 5|Jhn.5:5]], [[1-corinthians 2 3|1Co.2:3 15:43]], [[2-corinthians 12 9|2Co.12:9]]; pl., [[matthew 8 17|Mat.8:17]], [[luke 5 15|Luk.5:15 8:2]], [[2-corinthians 12 5|2Co.12:5 12:9-10]], [[1-timothy 5 23|1Ti.5:23]], [[hebrews 4 15|Heb.4:15]].† SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)

ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;] weakness, frailty, sickness: [[luke 13 11|Luk.13:11-12]], [[john 11 4|Jhn.11:4]], [[acts 28 9|Act.28:9]], [[romans 6 19|Rom.6:19 8:26]], [[2-corinthians 11 30|2Co.11:30 13:4]], [[galatians 4 13|Gal.4:13]] (MM, see word), [[hebrews 5 2|Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34]]; ἐν ἀ., [[john 5 5|Jhn.5:5]], [[1-corinthians 2 3|1Co.2:3 15:43]], [[2-corinthians 12 9|2Co.12:9]]; pl., [[matthew 8 17|Mat.8:17]], [[luke 5 15|Luk.5:15 8:2]], [[2-corinthians 12 5|2Co.12:5 12:9-10]], [[1-timothy 5 23|1Ti.5:23]], [[hebrews 4 15|Heb.4:15]].† SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)

ἀσθενέω, -ῶ ( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;] to be weak, feeble: [[acts 20 35|Act.20:35]], [[romans 8 3|Rom.8:3]], [[2-corinthians 11 21|2Co.11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9]]; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), [[romans 4 19|Rom.4:19 14:1]]; same implied, [[romans 14 2|Rom.14:2, 21]], [[1-corinthians 8 11|1Co.8:11-12]], [[2-corinthians 11 29|2Co.11:29]]; εἰς, [[2-corinthians 13 3|2Co.13:3.]] Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: [[matthew 25 36|Mat.25:36, 39]], [[luke 4 40|Luk.4:40]], [[john 4 46|Jhn.4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6]] [[acts 9 37|Act.9:37]], [[philippians 2 26|Php.2:26-27]], [[2-timothy 4 20|2Ti.4:20]], [[james 5 14|Jas.5:14]]; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: [[matthew 10 8|Mat.10:8]] (MM, see word), [[mark 6 56|Mrk.6:56]], [[luke 9 2|Luk.9:2]], [[acts 19 12|Act.19:12]].† (AS)

ἀσθενέω, -ῶ ( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;] to be weak, feeble: [[acts 20 35|Act.20:35]], [[romans 8 3|Rom.8:3]], [[2-corinthians 11 21|2Co.11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9]]; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), [[romans 4 19|Rom.4:19 14:1]]; same implied, [[romans 14 2|Rom.14:2, 21]], [[1-corinthians 8 11|1Co.8:11-12]], [[2-corinthians 11 29|2Co.11:29]]; εἰς, [[2-corinthians 13 3|2Co.13:3.]] Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: [[matthew 25 36|Mat.25:36, 39]], [[luke 4 40|Luk.4:40]], [[john 4 46|Jhn.4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6]] [[acts 9 37|Act.9:37]], [[philippians 2 26|Php.2:26-27]], [[2-timothy 4 20|2Ti.4:20]], [[james 5 14|Jas.5:14]]; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: [[matthew 10 8|Mat.10:8]] (MM, see word), [[mark 6 56|Mrk.6:56]], [[luke 9 2|Luk.9:2]], [[acts 19 12|Act.19:12]].† (AS)
ἀσθένημα, -τος, τό (ἀσθενής), an infirmity (MM, see word): [[romans 15 1|Rom.15:1.]]† (AS)

ἀσθενής -ές (ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;] without strength, weak, feeble: [[1-corinthians 1 27|1Co.1:27 4:10 12:22]], [[2-corinthians 10 10|2Co.10:10]], [[galatians 4 9|Gal.4:9]], [[1-thessalonians 5 14|1Th.5:14]], [[hebrews 7 18|Heb.7:18]], [[1-peter 3 7|1Pe.3:7]]. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: [[1-corinthians 1 25|1Co.1:25;]] of bodily debility, sick, sickly: [[matthew 25 39|Mat.25:39]] (Rec.) [[matthew 25 43|Mat.25:43-44]], [[luke 9 2|Luk.9:2]] (Rec.) [[luke 10 9|Luk.10:9]], [[acts 4 9|Act.4:9 5:15-16]] In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), [[matthew 26 41|Mat.26:41]], [[mark 14 38|Mrk.14:38]], [[romans 5 6|Rom.5:6]], [[1-corinthians 8 7|1Co.8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30]].† (AS)

ἀσθενής -ές (ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;] without strength, weak, feeble: [[1-corinthians 1 27|1Co.1:27 4:10 12:22]], [[2-corinthians 10 10|2Co.10:10]], [[galatians 4 9|Gal.4:9]], [[1-thessalonians 5 14|1Th.5:14]], [[hebrews 7 18|Heb.7:18]], [[1-peter 3 7|1Pe.3:7]]. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: [[1-corinthians 1 25|1Co.1:25;]] of bodily debility, sick, sickly: [[matthew 25 39|Mat.25:39]] (Rec.) [[matthew 25 43|Mat.25:43-44]], [[luke 9 2|Luk.9:2]] (Rec.) [[luke 10 9|Luk.10:9]], [[acts 4 9|Act.4:9 5:15-16]] In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), [[matthew 26 41|Mat.26:41]], [[mark 14 38|Mrk.14:38]], [[romans 5 6|Rom.5:6]], [[1-corinthians 8 7|1Co.8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30]].† (AS)
Ἀσιαός, -ή, -όν Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: [[acts 20 4|Act.20:4.]]† (AS)

Ἀσιάρχης, -ου, ὁ an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: [[acts 19 31|Act.19:31]] (Strab., Inscr.; DB, see word).† (AS)
ἀσιτία, -ας, ἡ (ἄσιτος), fasting, abstinence from food: [[acts 27 21|Act.27:21.]]† SYN.: νηστεία (MM, ut infr.) (AS)
ἄσιτος, -ον (ἀ- neg., σῖτος) fasting, without eating (cf. MM, see word): [[acts 27 33|Act.27:33.]]† (AS)
ἀσκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 2Ma.15:4 * ;] 1. to adorn (poët.). 2. to practise, exercise (Hdt., Xen.). 3. to endeavour (Xen., al.): with inf., [[acts 24 16|Act.24:16.]]† (AS)
ἀσκός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX for חֵמֶת, נֹאד, נֶבֶל ;] a leather bottle, wine-skin: [[matthew 9 17|Mat.9:17]], [[mark 2 22|Mrk.2:22]], [[luke 5 37|Luk.5:37-38]].† (AS)
ἀσμένως adv. (ἥδομαι, to be glad), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:12 2Mac 10:33, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 5:21 * ;] gladly: [[acts 21 17|Act.21:17.]]† (AS)
ἄ-σοθος, -ον [in LXX: [[proverbs 9 8|Pro.9:8]] א2 Α * ;] unwise, foolish: [[ephesians 5 15|Eph.5:15.]]† (AS)

ἀσπάζομαι depon., [in LXX: [[ezekiel 18 7|Eze.18:7]], [[judges 18 15|Jdg.18:15]] (שָׁלוֹם שָׁאַל), [[esther 5 2|Est.5:2]], 1Ma.7:29, al. ;] to welcome, greet, salute: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 5 47|Mat.5:47]], [[mark 9 15|Mrk.9:15]], [[acts 21 7|Act.21:7]], al.; id. before ἐν φιλήματι, [[romans 16 16|Rom.16:16]], [[1-corinthians 16 20|1Co.16:20]], [[2-corinthians 13 12|2Co.13:12]], [[1-thessalonians 5 26|1Th.5:26]], [[1-peter 5 14|1Pe.5:14]]; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), [[acts 18 22|Act.18:22;]] as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, see word), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), [[romans 16 22|Rom.16:22]] (on the aoristic Pres., here and elsewhere, see M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν . . . ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., see El., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), [[acts 25 13|Act.25:13]] (cf. ἀπ-ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).† (AS)

ἀσπασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἀσπάζομαι), a salutation (so always in RV), greeting: oral, [[matthew 23 7|Mat.23:7]], [[mark 12 38|Mrk.12:38]], [[luke 1 29|Luk.1:29, 41 1:44 11:43 20:46]]; written, [[1-corinthians 16 21|1Co.16:21]], [[colossians 4 18|Col.4:18]], [[2-thessalonians 3 17|2Th.3:17]].† (AS)

ἄ-σπιλος, -ον (ἀ- neg., σπῖλος) [in Sm.: [[job 15 15|Job.15:15]] (LXX, καθαρός)* ;] spotless, unstained: [[1-peter 1 19|1Pe.1:19;]] metaphorically, [[1-timothy 6 14|1Ti.6:14]], [[james 1 27|Jas.1:27]], [[2-peter 3 14|2Pe.3:14]] (for exx., see MM, see word).† SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄμωμος (AS)
ἀσπίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX for פֶּתֶן, etc. ;] an asp: [[romans 3 13|Rom.3:13.]]† (AS)
ἄσπονδος, -ον (σπονδή, a libation); 1. without truce (Thuc.). 2. admitting of no truce, implacable (Dem., al.): [[2-timothy 3 3|2Ti.3:3.]]† (AS)
ἀσσάριον, -ον, τό (diminutive of Lat. as), an assarion, a farthing, one-tenth of a drachma: [[matthew 10 29|Mat.10:29]], [[luke 12 6|Luk.12:6]] (MM, see word; DB, iii, 428; DCG, ii, 200).† (AS)
ἆσσον (Rec., after Vg., Ἄσσον), adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near), nearer: [[acts 27 13|Act.27:13]] (RV, close in shore; see B1., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).† (AS)
Ἄσσος, -ου (also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ή Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: [[acts 20 13|Act.20:13-14]] (see: ἆσσον).† (AS)

ἀστατέω, -ῶ (ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: [[isaiah 58 7|Isa.58:7]] (LXX, ἄστεγος)* ;] to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): [[1-corinthians 4 11|1Co.4:11]] † (AS)

ἀστεῖος, -ον (ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: [[exodus 2 2|Exo.2:2]] (טוֹב), [[numbers 22 32|Num.22:32]] (οὐκ ἀ. יָרַט), [[judges 3 17|Jdg.3:17]] (בָּרִיא), Jdth.11:23, Dan LXX, Sus 1:7, 2Ma.6:23 * ;] 1. of the town. 2. (Like Lat. urbanus), (a) courteous, (b) elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, see word), comely, fair (as in Ex, l.with), [[hebrews 11 23|Heb.11:23]], [[acts 7 20|Act.7:20]].† (AS)

ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;] a star: [[matthew 2 2|Mat.2:2, 7-10]] :, [[mark 13 25|Mrk.13:25]], [[1-corinthians 15 41|1Co.15:41]], [[revelation 6 13|Rev.6:13 8:10-12 9:1 12:1, 4]]; metaphorically, ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός [[revelation 2 28|Rev.2:28 22:16]]; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, [[revelation 1 16|Rev.1:16, 20 2:1 3:1]] (cf. ἄστρον, and see DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, see word).† (AS)
ἀ-στήρικτος, -ον (στηρίζω), unstable, unsettled: [[2-peter 2 14|2Pe.2:14 3:16]].† (AS)
ἄστοργος, -ον (στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, see: ἀγάπη) without natural affection: [[romans 1 31|Rom.1:31]], [[2-timothy 3 3|2Ti.3:3]] (MM, see word).† (AS)

ἀστοχέω, -ῶ (στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;] to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, [[1-timothy 1 6|1Ti.1:6]] (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, [[1-timothy 6 21|1Ti.6:21]], [[2-timothy 2 18|2Ti.2:18]].† (AS)

ἀστραπή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for בָּרָק ;] lightning: [[matthew 24 27|Mat.24:27 28:3]], [[luke 10 18|Luk.10:18 17:24]]; pl., [[revelation 4 5|Rev.4:5 8:5 11:19 16:18]]; of a lamp, shining brightness, [[luke 11 36|Luk.11:36.]]† (AS)
ἀστράπτω [in LXX for בָּרָק ;] to lighten, flash forth: [[luke 17 24|Luk.17:24 24:4]] (MM, see word).† (AS)

ἄστρον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;] (a) mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: [[luke 21 25|Luk.21:25]], [[acts 27 20|Act.27:20]], [[hebrews 11 12|Heb.11:12]]; (b) in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, [[acts 7 43|Act.7:43]] (cf. ἀστήρ, and see MM, see word).† (AS)
Ἀσύνκριτος (Rec. Ἀσύγκρ.), -ου, ὁ Asyncritus: [[romans 16 14|Rom.16:14.]]† (AS)
